- Original source: [Robin Hood](https://www.gamesurf.it/recensioni/gioco/robin-hood-c7493)
- Author / publication: Gamesurf Staff; GameSurf.
- Language / date: Italian; 2002-12-02.

- Checked: 2026-09-09

- Format: header notes, original summary, then complete factual notes (commercial review, not transcribed)

The reviewer argues that the opening mission initially makes the game look too similar to Commandos, while later play reveals greater freedom and multiple solutions. The inspected passage discusses avoiding guards, rationing arrows, paying beggars for information, using buildings, and provoking fights among soldiers with money bags.

The verdict gives 8/10 and praises original ideas and reduced frustration for newcomers. This is useful contemporary evidence of how the game’s early learning curve could obscure its broader systems..

## Detailed notes

Page facts: title "Robin Hood" (section: Recensioni); byline "di Gamesurf Staff"; dated 02 dicembre 2002 23:00; score box "8 / Voto / Redazione" with a closing verdict paragraph; retrieved directly from gamesurf.it. Page 1 was retrieved first; pages 2 to 4 were retrieved in a second pass and are covered below (the review has four pages; the page-5 link repeats page 1). Italian commercial review, not transcribed.

Page 1 content, in order:

- Opening thesis: the game "astonishes, disorients and gives a wrong idea of its quality" unless played with due care and patience. Calling it a simple Commandos clone is "the most wrong thing there is"; several hours are needed to discover the full potential of its gameplay. The game gives much freedom of action and different ways to solve the same mission.
- Section "Un clone di Commandos?": the game most resembling it is certainly Commandos, evident from the first session. The hero moves on a "really large" two-dimensional map trying mainly not to be noticed by guards. Shared points: escaping notice when outside a guard's field of view (shown by "the usual green cone"); actions such as jumping, running, walking silently, stunning a guard, fighting.
- Each mission is "a small, ingenious puzzle": castle corridors, villages, helping the poor, dozens of well-armed guards with an AI described as "incredibly realistic" (to be discussed later in the review). It is not an arcade game for a joypad but a strategy game where, as in Commandos, every action must be planned.
- Section "La prima missione: tutto qui?": after some tens of minutes the first mission initially disappointed the reviewers through excessive similarity to Commandos and the hero's limited actions; frustration was comparable (a castle full of guards and archers). In the first mission Robin can only stun guards from behind or fight, which made the game seem unappealing at first; "never stop at first appearances".
- First mission objective as described: discover where an ally is. It teaches silent movement and that eluding a guard beats fighting one, especially when alone.
- Robin's other actions listed: shooting arrows at distant enemies ("arrows are never many, so beware"), giving alms to beggars to obtain valuable information, hiding inside houses, using bags of coins to distract soldiers.
- The coin-bag trick is called "really hilarious": thrown at a large group of guards, they gradually brawl, calling each other "thief"; a few coins can dispose of a sizeable squad.
- An image table placeholder (images 4, 5, 6) precedes the pagination.

Verdict box (page 1, "Redazione", score 8): "a Signor Gioco" (a real game); the inheritance from Commandos is evident, but it offers original and interesting ideas and a lower level of frustration that will please genre newcomers and the impatient.

### Pages 2 to 4, added from continuation retrievals

Retrieved directly from gamesurf.it on 2026-09-09. The review is four pages long; the "page-5" URL returned page 1 again, so the earlier "5 pages" reading was wrong. The same score box (8, Redazione) repeats on every page.

Page 2, section "Seconda missione: come rimangiarsi tutto" (second mission: eating one's words):
- From the second mission the earlier impressions (frustration, little originality) prove wrong. Saving a friend from the gallows gives a party of men who obey orders, plus new actions.
- Where Robin could only stun a guard for a few minutes, the new men can tie a guard up or even kill him. A soldier who finds a tied guard immediately raises the alarm and unties him; he cannot do that with a dead one. Killing everyone would therefore seem logical, but it forfeits the population's favour, "which plays an extremely important role".
- The first mission is thus revealed as a training taste. Recruits fall into categories, each able to perform only certain operations; a varied party is essential. Actions listed: throwing nets to immobilise guards; using apples to distract them; archers; healers who restore energy with medicinal herbs; men who pick locks. Special characters Lady Marian, Will Scarlet, Little John "and others" have unique traits.
- Section "Le risorse prime" (raw materials): after every mission from the second onward the player returns to the base camp in Sherwood. There men can be assigned to make arrows and traps, look for medicinal herbs, and train in fencing and archery, a managerial layer the reviewer says adds realism and atmosphere absent from similar titles. Before a mission (often selectable) the player chooses who to bring and who stays to gather resources. Ambushing twenty armed guards without a single arrow or trap is possible "but decidedly inadvisable". Recruits can grow mission by mission but it is tied to behaviour and reputation: kill many guards needlessly and hardly anyone will join "a ferocious brigand".

Page 3, section "Le missioni":
- Mission count given as "oltre 30" (over 30), based on castle infiltrations (freeing prisoners, meeting Lady Marian), defensive missions, and convoy attacks to raise funds. Castle missions have varied, never obvious objectives: avoiding patrols, scaling walls, hiding in rooms, surprising guards from behind.
- Compared with Commandos the game is less frustrating and more playable for newcomers; being discovered and forced to fight still leaves a chance to win, which rarely happened in Commandos. Thoughtless play that kills all guards yields poor reputation and no new recruits.
- Fidelity to the hero's spirit: fighting while jumping onto a table, agile dodging of a guard, climbing curtain walls, jumping across rooftops to reach a bonus.
- Ambush missions (robbing a gold shipment or a rich merchant): pre-placed traps in the scenery (pits, hidden nets) plus companions ready to act; traps are triggered by shooting small circles with arrows, which sounds easy "but arrows are always scarce", and traps never suffice to disable all soldiers.
- Every mission can be completed in different ways, giving long replayability. Example from the reviewers' play: in an ambush they lured the bulk of the escort away from the cart and then eliminated the two guards left near it. Eliminating all soldiers is never required.
- Guard AI: they brawl over coins thrown near them and flee to call reinforcements when outnumbered.

Page 4, sections "Combattimenti con arma bianca" (melee combat) and "Grafica e sonoro":
- Ranged combat with bow and arrows; sword duels with one or more guards are controlled with the mouse via a thrust-and-parry system driven by mouse buttons and quick movements, "not always practical". A finishing blow requires drawing a reversed figure eight; a circular blow a circular movement, "etc.". Problems appear in the most frantic fights or when characters are partly hidden by background elements. Advice: avoid unequal fights and play cunningly.
- Technical: fully 2D, no textures or polygons, so a 3D accelerator is not essential. Forests, castles and forest assaults show surprising care for detail; landscapes look almost like paintings. Character animations are well made and varied; zooming in is possible (the background grains noticeably), as is a panoramic view. Even on not-so-recent computers 800x600 or 1024x768 give good scrolling fluidity.
- Sound uses Creative EAX libraries but has flaws: lip sync in cutscenes is not always correct and people's comments tend to repeat. The full Italian localisation of all dialogue is praised as always well acted.
- Conclusion: built on the elements that made Commandos famous, with greater variety of action, managerial elements and less frustration; "a title to buy with eyes closed".
